Replaces repeated 'no implementation detail' verdict with a specific gap; advances rather than restates.
Names the competitive pressure with sourced context; 'they find one' payoff preserved.
Replaces three restatements of price/speed conclusion with the accuracy question raised at line 61 but never resolved; keeps the sourced uncertainty.
Replaces repeated 'public data mitigates severity' restatement with the policy-escalation consequence that follows from line 98.
Replaces three-story bullet recap with a single connecting idea; preserves actionable closes without repeating individual story verdicts.

scenes.chemistry: Strong in places — the 'one notch' exchange and Rufus/Jamie on institutional memory land well. The Jamie-revises-alarm moment is genuinely earned.
scenes.discovery: The building-sales detail is surfaced naturally and pays off. Advisory-council risk is developed through conversation rather than summary.
scenes.repetition: Lines 41 and 47 both restate 'we don't know the implementation / won't know for years' after the point has already settled at line 48. Line 40 ('That's diplomatic') echoes line 23 too closely.

scenes.chemistry: The sports-car/commute exchange (78-81) is the best trio moment in the segment. Context-window explanation flows naturally between all three.
scenes.discovery: Terra-as-product-tier read (line 77) is Jamie's strongest original observation. Computer-use angle developed across multiple turns rather than stated once.
scenes.repetition: Lines 82-83 restate the cost/speed conclusion already established at lines 53-55 and 64. Line 84 then adds a third restatement of the same point about mid-tier adoption.

scenes.chemistry: The contractor/warehouse analogy (113-117) is the sharpest scene in the episode. Rufus's 'initiative' line (103) earns a genuine beat. Jamie's facilities-management tease (118) lands cleanly.
scenes.discovery: The distinction between permissions architecture and value alignment (104-105) is the episode's clearest analytical advance. White House disclosure as policy escalator is well handled.
scenes.repetition: Line 110 re-explains the 'public data mitigates severity' argument that was already resolved at lines 106-108. No new evidence added.

scenes.chemistry: Closing loop on the Dutch question works. Rufus's honest hedge (122) is appropriately non-conclusive. Jamie's 'real skepticism, not about the ambition' is well-phrased.
scenes.discovery: The 2027 figure as near-term test was already named in segment 2 (line 48); its reappearance here as the closer is earned because it's now the editorial verdict rather than a prediction.
scenes.repetition: Lines 126-128 list all three stories' conclusions sequentially in a way that recaps rather than closes. The 'who wins' framing repeats the Dutch and Terra conclusions without adding consequence.

review_before_repairs.rufus_feature: The Wall Street dispatch (lines 57-59) opens well — 'the quieter trading floor, mostly monitors' — but the studio exchange after the return is missing. Jamie's accuracy challenge (line 60) and Rufus's concession (line 61) function as a responsive exchange, but they are not marked or framed as a return from the feature; they read as ordinary segment dialogue. The imagined scene needs a cleaner return beat so the feature has a distinct arc.
remaining_issues: Lines 82-84 restate the Terra price/speed conclusion three times after it was established at lines 53-55; replace with a sourced exchange on the accuracy question that was flagged but not answered.
Line 110 reopens the 'public data mitigates severity' argument without new evidence; cut or replace with the policy-escalation consequence.
Lines 126-128 close by listing all three story conclusions as bullet-point recap rather than landing on a single consequential idea; trim the recap and sharpen the ending.
The Rufus feature lacks an explicit return marker and a brief studio exchange before the segment resumes; needs one anchoring return line.
Line 40 ('That's diplomatic') repeats the same beat as line 23 ('That's generous') too closely within the same scene.
